challengeFindings.title: A consumer with lint-staged installed and no root lint-staged config upgrades, the sync deletes `.bkit/templates/.lintstagedrc.json` (the only config lint-staged found), and every later commit fails in pre-commit with "Configuration could not be found"

A workflow or prompt can now name `.prettierignore` or `.lintstagedrc.json` (an adopted-template path) and the template-path guard stays green, because the forbidden names derive from template file names and the rename dropped both destination names

An agent editing bkit's own `.bkit/templates/prettierignore.example` or `lintstagedrc.example.json` gets the generic checklist instead of the gate-config advisory, because `GATE_CONFIG_PATTERNS` match only the old dotfile basenames, while the hook comment says bkit's template source "stays guarded"

The adoption audit's reconcile step runs `diff .bkit/templates/<path> <path>`, which for the renamed samples diffs against a root `prettierignore.example` / `lintstagedrc.example.json` that never exists, and its merged check runs `git log` on a path whose history starts at the upgrade commit, so an adopted `.prettierignore` reads as unreconciled or pending

challengeFindings.title: A consumer that commits through husky + lint-staged, relied on the nested sample and never copied `scripts/prettier/bkit-insert-ignore.mjs`, upgrades; the migration's root `.lintstagedrc.json` now claims every staged file, so the next bkit workflow commit that stages `docs/plans/**/*.md` runs `node scripts/prettier/bkit-insert-ignore.mjs`, which does not exist, and the pre-commit hook fails every such commit

A consumer whose own commit config is `lint-staged.config.ts` (or `.lintstagedrc.ts` / `.mts` / `.cts`, `lint-staged.config.mts` / `.cts`, or a `lint-staged` key in `package.yaml`) upgrades; `hasLintStagedConfig` does not know those names, so the migration writes `.lintstagedrc.json` beside it, and lint-staged, which sorts same-folder configs alphabetically and gives each folder to the first, silently runs bkit's sample instead of the consumer's own tasks

Every consumer that never adopted lint-staged gets an unrequested `.lintstagedrc.json` at its root on upgrade, and the "Quick tidy-up on commit" tip stops firing, because install seeds `bkit:gate:format` = `pnpm lint-staged` into every consumer, so the migration's gate check is true for all of them and nothing checks that lint-staged is installed

`bkit install` on a consumer in the trigger state records `.lintstagedrc.json` in `.bkit/version` `canonicalHashes`, so a copy-and-own file the consumer is told to adapt is tracked as a bkit-managed file, because the install path pushes the write without `unhashed: true`
